memory_candidates.content: When discriminating a 'draft-history version label' pattern from a 'durable, legitimate version axis' pattern (e.g. a schema/file-format document self-declaring its own format version in a heading, vs. a decision record narrating its own prior draft), a plain v[0-9]-token regex cannot tell them apart -- both look identical at the token level. The discriminator that worked: check whether the vN token is inside (or immediately follows) a backtick-quoted code span naming an identifier/filename ('`book.toml` v2', '`book-evidence-observation-v1`', '`-v2`' filename fragments) -- a schema document naming itself this way is durable axis (file-format version), while a bare heading or Status-line vN with no such code-span anchor is the forbidden page-level label. Verified live: this exact ambiguity produced 5 false positives in a real corpus before the backtick-anchor check was added.

When building a detection/classification pattern library against a real-world corpus (lint rules, discriminators, etc.), run the live calibration pass AS EARLY AS POSSIBLE -- even ahead of the plan's nominal 'calibration phase' -- rather than writing the full pattern set first and validating later. In this task, pulling the calibration into the same phase as initial pattern authorship surfaced 2 real discriminator misses immediately, while the patterns were still cheap to change; deferring validation to a later phase would have meant re-opening already-'frozen' pattern variables.
